newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Friday with shortcovering by manufacturers for RSS3 rubber nudging prices higher although the mood remained quiet because of the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, dealers said.
"We saw some shortcovering this morning, mainly for RSS3 rubber. But the market became quiet in the afternoon when everybody left for an early vacation," a Singapore-based rubber trader said.
Some 825 tonnes of the July/September 1997 RSS3 contract was bought while 600 tonnes of the April/June 1997 TSR20 contract was also sold in the local exchange.
All months in the RSS1 contract in the exchange were untraded.
"The volumes in the market were still thin. It was not particularly spectacular," one dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, July/September RSS3 was seen unchanged at 130.50 U.S. cents a kg.
January RSS1 was indicated steady at 179.50 Singapore cents (US$1.28) a kg.
July/September TSR20 was seen also steady at 178.50 Singapore cents (US$1.27) a kg.
